hints.title: Find both angles with each sine
hints.body: For each given sine value, take the acute angle and its supplement. Use the ordering of x and y to compare the two acute angles.
hints.recap: An acute angle and its supplement have the same sine.
hints.pitfall: Both acute and obtuse angles can occur in a triangle.
hints.pause: Write the two choices for A and the two choices for B.

recall.reminder: An acute angle and its supplement have the same sine.

hints.title: Test the angle pairs
hints.body: Pair each choice for A with each choice for B. A valid triangle must leave a positive third angle.
hints.recap: The interior angles of a triangle sum to 180 degrees.
hints.pitfall: A sum of exactly 180 degrees gives a flat shape, not a triangle.
hints.pause: Check all the pairs using the order of the acute angles.

recall.reminder: The interior angles of a triangle sum to 180 degrees.

hints.title: Check whether the triangles are distinct
hints.body: For each valid angle pair, use the fixed side to decide whether the triangle is determined. Then compare the angle sets of the resulting triangles.
hints.recap: Two angles and the side between them determine a triangle up to congruence.
hints.pitfall: The same triangle turned over is not a new triangle.
hints.pause: Decide the possible counts, and whether the count changes with x and y.

recall.reminder: Two angles and the side between them determine a triangle up to congruence.

solution:
Write α=sin−1x, β=sin−1y with 0<α<β<90∘. The acute pair (α,β) is valid. The pair (α,180∘−β) is also valid because its sum is 180∘−(β−α)<180∘.

The pair (180∘−α,β) has sum greater than 180∘, and two obtuse angles are impossible. Each of the two valid pairs fixes one triangle with AB=1.

The triangles are not congruent: the second has obtuse angle 180∘−β. If the first had that same angle, its third angle 180∘−α−β would equal it, forcing α=0, which is excluded.

Exactly two non-congruent triangles always result, so only statement II is possible: C.
knowledgePattern: Exhaust acute/obtuse angle choices with a fixed side
